manifest.name: dsh-page-zoom
manifest.description: Page zoom for DeepSeek Harness: Ctrl + mouse wheel scales the whole UI in 5% steps (30%–200%), with a magnifier percentage readout in the bottom-right corner.
manifest.author: Centaurea5547196

bundle.text:
# dsh-page-zoom bundle layer.
#
# Inserts one roster row. The package declares `dsh.client` (platform: web), so
# the dsh-client-modules node half serves lib/client.js as a browser plugin at
# /plugins/dsh-page-zoom/client.js.
- insert:
    - id: page-zoom
      name: 'dsh-page-zoom'

readme.text:
Page zoom for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) / DSH Desktop.

Hold **Ctrl** and scroll the mouse wheel to scale the entire interface — sidebar, menus, settings, overlays and conversation alike. A magnifier glyph with the current percentage sits in the bottom-right corner.

English | [简体中文](README.zh.md)

| Gesture | Result |
|---|---|
| `Ctrl` + mouse wheel up | Zoom in one step |
| `Ctrl` + mouse wheel down | Zoom out one step |

- Step: **5%** per wheel notch
- Range: **30% – 200%**
- The level is remembered (`localStorage`), so it survives a reload.

There are no buttons, no menus and no keyboard shortcuts — the readout is display-only.

- Bottom-right corner, **12px / 10px** from the edges.
- **A magnifier glyph, then the number.** A bare `100%` in a corner means nothing
  on its own; the glyph is the convention browsers and phones already use for
  this exact reading.
- Display only: `pointer-events: none`, so it never intercepts a click and never
  gets in the way of the UI underneath.
- No box, no border, no background — it borrows the app's own font stack
  (`--dsw-font-family`) and its muted tertiary label colour
  (`--dsw-alias-label-tertiary`), so it reads as part of the chrome rather than
  as a floating widget.
- **Scaled with the page, not against it.** The readout grows and shrinks with
  everything else, and so does its gap from the corner, so it stays proportional
  to the app's own layout: 47×13 at 100%, 93×26 at 200%, 12×4 at 30%. Whatever it
  does not cover at 100%, it does not cover at 200% either.

This works without any arithmetic because a fixed box's visual offset is the
  declared value multiplied by its own `zoom` **and** by every ancestor `zoom`.
  Keeping the element's zoom at 1 and the declared inset constant is therefore
  already linear in the page zoom. Multiplying the value by the level as well
  makes it quadratic — a declared 24px renders as 48px at 200%.
- `role="img"` with an `aria-label`, deliberately **not** `role="status"`.
  `status` is a live region, so a screen reader would interrupt with
  "Page zoom 105%", "Page zoom 110%" on every wheel notch.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:Centaurea5547196/dsh-page-zoom
dsh plugin --profile web     add github:Centaurea5547196/dsh-page-zoom
```

If `git` is not available on the machine, install from the release tarball
instead — `dsh` accepts a remote archive spec:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add https://github.com/Centaurea5547196/dsh-page-zoom/archive/refs/heads/main.tar.gz
```

Zoom is the CSS `zoom` property set on the document element, **not**
`transform: scale`. `zoom` reflows layout exactly like the browser's own zoom, so
fixed-position chrome keeps working. `transform` would leave fixed elements
clipped and would additionally turn the root into a containing block for every
`position: fixed` descendant.

DeepSeek Harness ships no page zoom of its own: the only typography setting is
`ui-theme.fontSize`, which affects conversation body text only — sidebar labels,
menus and settings chrome are fixed pixel sizes. This plugin adds the missing
gesture.

The listener sits on `window` in the **bubble** phase with `{ passive: false }`,
and it yields to any surface that already claimed the event
(`event.defaultPrevented`). That ordering matters: the sidebar's document preview
binds its own cursor-anchored Ctrl+wheel zoom on its scrollport and calls
`preventDefault()`. A capture-phase listener on `document` would fire before that
handler ever ran, and `stopPropagation()` there would kill the preview's zoom
outright. Being last in line keeps the preview working while every other surface
still falls through to page zoom. It also overrides the browser's native zoom
when the Harness is opened in a plain browser tab.

The whole thing is plain DOM — no React surface, no host-side code, no network
access, no storage beyond one `localStorage` key.
